reagents.name: NaBH4
reagents.whatItDoes: Reduces aldehydes and ketones to alcohols. Does NOT reduce esters, amides, or carboxylic acids.

reagents.name: LiAlH4
reagents.whatItDoes: Strong hydride reducer: reduces aldehydes, ketones, esters, carboxylic acids, amides, nitriles, epoxides.
reagents.conditions: Anhydrous Et2O or THF; acidic workup

reagents.name: DIBAL-H
reagents.whatItDoes: Selective 1-equivalent reducer. At −78 °C with 1 eq, stops ester reduction at the aldehyde.

reagents.name: PCC
reagents.whatItDoes: Mild oxidant. 1° alcohols → aldehydes (stops there). 2° alcohols → ketones.

reagents.name: Jones (CrO3/H2SO4)
reagents.whatItDoes: Strong oxidant. 1° alcohols → carboxylic acids. 2° alcohols → ketones.

reagents.name: NBS
reagents.whatItDoes: Benzylic / allylic bromination via radicals. Supplies low [Br2].

reagents.name: Sn/HCl (or Fe/HCl, H2/Pd)
reagents.fullName: Tin or iron in acid; also H2/Pd
reagents.whatItDoes: Reduces aromatic nitro groups to primary amines.
reagents.conditions: HCl aqueous; basic workup liberates ArNH2

reagents.name: CuBr / CuCl / CuCN (Sandmeyer)
reagents.whatItDoes: Replace ArN2+ with Br, Cl, or CN. Also H3PO2 → H, HBF4/heat → F (Schiemann).
reagents.conditions: Ar-N2+ first prepared from Ar-NH2 + NaNO2/HCl at 0 °C

reagents.name: Lindlar / H2
reagents.fullName: Pd on CaCO3, poisoned with Pb and quinoline
reagents.whatItDoes: Alkyne → Z-alkene (cis). Stops at the alkene; does not over-reduce.

reagents.name: Na / NH3(l)
reagents.whatItDoes: Alkyne → E-alkene (trans). Also reduces aromatic rings (Birch) under proper conditions.
reagents.conditions: Liquid NH3, Na metal; EtOH co-solvent for Birch

reagents.name: Ph3P=CR2 (Wittig)
reagents.whatItDoes: Converts aldehydes and ketones to alkenes via oxaphosphetane; byproduct Ph3P=O.
reagents.conditions: THF, room temperature. Made from Ph3P + alkyl halide + strong base (n-BuLi).

reagents.name: LDA
reagents.whatItDoes: Strong, bulky, non-nucleophilic base. Generates the KINETIC enolate at −78 °C.

reagents.name: NaOMe / NaOEt (equilibrating)
reagents.whatItDoes: Equilibrating base — forms the THERMODYNAMIC enolate (more substituted).

reagents.name: H3O+ (dilute)
reagents.whatItDoes: Protonates alkoxides/carbanions after a nucleophilic addition; hydrolyzes imines, acetals, enol ethers.

reagents.name: SOCl2
reagents.whatItDoes: Converts carboxylic acids to acyl chlorides; alcohols to alkyl chlorides.
reagents.conditions: Neat or in CH2Cl2; pyridine to scavenge HCl

reagents.name: NaCN (SN2 then hydrolyze)
reagents.whatItDoes: SN2 on 1° alkyl halide → R-CN (one-carbon homologation). Hydrolyze to R-COOH.

reagents.name: NaBH3CN
reagents.whatItDoes: Mild hydride source for reductive amination. Reduces iminium ions preferentially over C=O at mildly acidic pH.

reagents.name: NaOH (saponification)
reagents.whatItDoes: Hydrolyzes esters to carboxylate + alcohol (irreversible, driven by deprotonation).

reagents.name: Br2 / FeBr3 (EAS)
reagents.whatItDoes: Electrophilic aromatic bromination of benzene and activated arenes.
reagents.conditions: CH2Cl2 or neat; stoichiometric Br2, catalytic FeBr3

reagents.name: HNO3 / H2SO4 (nitration)
reagents.fullName: Nitric acid in sulfuric acid (generates NO2+)
reagents.whatItDoes: Electrophilic aromatic nitration.

reagents.name: AlCl3 (Friedel–Crafts)
reagents.whatItDoes: Lewis acid catalyst for Friedel–Crafts acylation (RCOCl) and alkylation (RCl).

reagents.name: NaNH2
reagents.whatItDoes: Very strong base. Deprotonates terminal alkynes; triggers E2 and benzyne formation.
